findings.title: Successor historical fixture family is unnamed in the derived inventory
findings.evidence: Owner map §6 keeps tests/fixtures/phase-3a1b-freeze-successor-v1/{successor-contract.json,successor-contract-type.ts,successor-test-context.ts,temporary-repository-harness.mjs,controlled-freeze-successor.mjs,analyzers/workflow/routing-analyzer.ts} as historical evidence and tells current consumers to drop live routing/hash use. Those paths are not in any of the seven policy inventories and are not in helpers[], so inventory.json neither marks them preserved-input nor lists successor-contract.json currentSha256 pins of editable tests (gossip/work/operation files at successor-contract.json:90-101,144-152). The successor RED file is editable, so GREEN can still follow the owner map, but the frozen inventory does not mechanically forbid restamping those historical currentSha256/currentBlob fields. Walk also only matches path+sha256 or path-keyed sha256, not currentSha256.
findings.violated_requirement: Complete inventory classification; no opportunistic restamp of historical evidence after RED begins

findings.title: Schema property insertion order is compressed relative to the live bijection
findings.evidence: README says add authorShareMultiplier and keep declaration order plus seven required names. Live registry parameters.fields lists the optional multiplier first (registry-v1.json:55-66). The retained bijection oracle requires schema $defs.parameters.properties keys to equal that registry field order (registry-spec-n1prime-b.test.ts:491-497). Owner map §7 states the same. An implementer who only appends the property would fail that existing oracle, so this is wording tightness, not a missing consumer.
findings.violated_requirement: Schema catch-up must match registry declaration order while keeping seven required names
